30 Two positive charges and one negative charge, all of equal magnitude, are set at the corners of
an equilateral triangle.
Which diagram best represents the electric field surrounding the charges?
A
B
–
–
+
+
+
+
C
D
–
–
+
+
+
+

hints: Notice the two $+$ charges at the base and the $-$ charge at the top - field lines must leave a $+$ and arrive at a $-$.
Count the net charge as $+Q +Q -Q = +Q$, so some lines from the $+$ charges cannot end on the single $-$ and must go off to infinity.
Look for curved lines joining each bottom $+$ directly to the top $-$ as well as outer lines leaving to infinity, and reject any diagram with closed loops.
walkthrough: Identify the set-up: two equal $+$ charges at the bottom corners and one equal $-$ charge at the top corner of the equilateral triangle.
State the field-line rules: lines leave positive charges and enter negative charges, never cross, and never form closed loops in electrostatics.
Between the charges, many lines must go directly from each $+$ to the nearby $-$, giving the curved links on the left and right sides.
Check infinity: total charge is positive, so the $-$ cannot absorb all lines from two $+$ charges and some lines from the $+$ charges must escape outward to infinity.
Only the diagram with inward arrows at the top $-$, outward arrows at the bottom $+$ charges, direct $+$ to $-$ curves, and outer lines to infinity satisfies all rules. This is option A.

A.explanation: Field lines leave each $+$ charge, enter the $-$ charge, and some leave to infinity because net charge is $+Q$.

B.explanation: Lines leave the $+$ charges and enter the $-$ charge but it omits the curved field lines that go directly from each $+$ to the $-$.

C.explanation: Closed loops are shown, but electric field lines must start on $+$ or infinity and end on $-$ or infinity, never form closed loops.

D.explanation: Closed loops are shown around all three charges, which is impossible for electrostatic field lines from point charges.
